beta_new: Follow a crack up to the horizontal break, then continue on the face past a pair of bolts.
Three bolts lead to a ledge on the tower's east side, and the higher section of that side is then climbed with two more bolts.
On the southwest face, work leftward up a flake and ledge system, then continue past a horizontal break and a single bolt to the summit.
A direct line up the face with two bolts leads to the belay of Twinkle Toes. Beginning instead at the start of the Twinkle Toes traverse makes the lead safer.
Low on the route, beware a big loose block, and treat the bolt ladder with suspicion since the bolts are in poor shape.
Medium to large cams in the lower chimney make the opening safer; higher, four bolts take you to the top.

moves.from: Medium to large cams in the lower chimney

value.text: Medium to large cams for the lower chimney.

beta_new: Climb the wall below the biggest chockstone clipping two bolts, then exit through the big opening at mid-height and clip three more bolts to a belay with two bolts.
Follows the line of bolts directly upward along the rock's right-hand edge, then eases off by trending leftward onto easier ground.
Begin in the corner and drift slightly rightward, eventually mounting a chunkier face. Expect technical climbing with six bolts along the way.
Start up a curving chimney that leads to a ledge equipped with rappel anchors (Bat Ledge), then follow the obvious crack overhead.
Climb to the first bolt, shuffle left along a horizontal crack, then continue up past a second bolt. How hard it feels depends on your height.
Climbs the boulder's east arete, starting from a neighboring boulder, with a lone bolt around mid-height.
Begin out on the upper ledge's right-hand extremity and follow the right-hand arete of the highest summit. The face is overhanging, and the crux falls between bolts four and five.
Technical moves matter more than strength here. Start on the crack's left side, clip three bolts, then step across the crack to the right for the final two bolts.
Technical moves matter more than strength here. Start on the crack's left side, clip three bolts, then step across the crack to the right for the final two bolts.
Share the opening twenty feet with Beautiful Dreamer, then, stepping left, clip a bolt and pass three fixed pins before reaching the bolted rap station.
Four bolts protect the line; after the third, cut sharply rightward to gain the final one.
The crux comes right at the start: boulder up from the base to reach a crack tilting leftward that stops short of the ground. A single bolt sits near the top.

moves.from: A single bolt sits near the top.

beta_new: Start up a crack, then step rightward onto plates and climb past three bolts, although the third bolt appears to be absent.

Begin at the first bolt of the neighboring Shoveling Coal line and trend rightward past a pair of bolts, reaching a belay beneath a plated pillar. Ascend it to its top, traverse left along horizontal cracks, and finish up another crack.
Heading straight up to the first bolt is the harder way; starting from the left makes the opening easier. The route has two bolts.
A finesse line where strength is unnecessary. Mono pockets appear on the way, though using them is optional, and six bolts lead to an anchor shared with another route.
Climbing the right-hand crack system, a bolt about twenty feet up marks the spot to swap from the right-hand crack over into a left-hand one.
Step off a boulder and follow a sequence of cracks slanting rightward, clipping a bolt on the way and ending in one more rightward-slanting crack.
Opens on a brief crack and continues as face climbing past two bolts; a thorny cat's claw bush grows beside the start and must be negotiated.

moves.from: Bring large protection, as the offwidth and chimney take gear up to about six inches.

value.text: Bring large protection; the offwidth and chimney take gear up to about six inches.

beta_new: Follow the barely formed crack upward, clipping two bolts on the way.
From inside a large cave, the line moves onto overhanging rock with four bolts.

moves.from: ; carry a few natural pieces as well.

value.text: Carry a few natural pieces as well.

beta_new: Reachy and mentally engaging, with a hard, dynamic crux just above the second bolt. Seven bolts lead to the anchor, and the stone here is volcanic tuff.
A big high step and slapping between slopers carry you past the crux, found just beyond the third bolt.

The hardest climbing is low, from the ground to above the second bolt, and the base holds have been worn smooth on soft sandy rock.

Another tough move waits on your right once the final bolt is clipped; should you still have energy at the anchor, continue rightward up the upper bolts of Earthcling.
Easy ground leads up to bolt one, after which the route surmounts a steep bulge close beneath the top edge.
Begin among the bushes at the foot of the wall and work up the face next to Yucca Bowl; the bolts that once protected it are gone.
Two bolts lead up, then the line merges with the adjacent route where that route has its fourth bolt.
Work up the dike until it forks into a pair, with two bolts for protection along the way.
Ascend the left-facing corner, then step rightward by a bolt to enter a finger crack that ends at a bolted belay. Shift right again to another bolt and finish up a crack.
Along the southern side, work up a faint corner that faces right, clipping a bolt near the top.
Begin on the gully-ledge that slopes rightward and upward, move left, then continue straight past the bolts.
The hardest moves come between bolts one and three on juggy, steep rock. Veering left rather than right after the first clip makes the route noticeably easier.
Once on Crystal Palace Ledge via the ramp, work up the dihedral all the way to its end, then trace the Crystal Corner leftward with bat hooks plus bolts to a two-bolt stance.
